rules_sent_back.instruction: Use bpmn:userTask for human work assisted by software and bpmn:manualTask for human work performed without an execution application.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person makes a choice among options presented to them, and names no software or system that the person uses to make that choice

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person selects or decides among the options offered, and mentions no software, form, system, or electronic step for that choice: Model the human choice as a manualTask in the lane of the person who makes it, not as a userTask. Reserve userTask for activities the description says are carried out with software or a system.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person selects or decides among the options offered, and mentions no software, form, system, or electronic step for that choice

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists a step of waiting for an outcome as one ordered step in a sequence and names no message, signal, timer or condition for that wait: Model that waiting step as a task placed in the sequence at its stated position. Use an intermediate catch event only where the description names a message, signal, timer or condition that the process waits for.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says information is gathered from an outside party (such as a company) as one ordered step, and it names no message that is sent or awaited for that gathering

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several steps that the process itself performs for the person, such as fetching or collecting information, checking that gathered material is complete, preparing documents, or applying for a benefit, placed between choices, notifications, or waits: Model each such described step as its own activity in the order the description gives, and do not omit it or fold it into a neighboring activity. Use a serviceTask when the description attributes the step to a system, and a manualTask when it attributes the step to a person. Keep the dependency the description states, so that a later choice or notification follows the step it depends on.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several steps that the process itself performs for the person, such as fetching or collecting information, checking that gathered material is complete, preparing documents, or applying for a benefit, placed between choices, notifications, or waits

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities that are carried out concurrently or in no stated order, and a later step starts only after all of them have completed: Model these activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway (split) before them, with one outgoing branch per activity and no conditions on the branches. Merge the branches with a matching parallel gateway (join) placed before the later step, so that step starts only after every branch has completed. Do not order the activities arbitrarily, do not use an exclusive gateway for the split or join, and do not let the later step follow any single branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several activities that are carried out concurrently or in no stated order, and a later step starts only after all of them have completed
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines GW-05), generalized from EXS-022

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person chooses one of several options that were first retrieved, and later steps depend on the option chosen: Model the retrieval of the candidate options as its own activity. Model the choice as a separate activity performed by the person named in the description, placed after the retrieval and before the activities that depend on the choice. Keep the retrieval and the choice as distinct elements, and do not add activities for consequences the description does not state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person chooses one of several options that were first retrieved, and later steps depend on the option chosen
